articles.summary: The Kroger Co. (NYSE: KR), America's grocer, today announced that six wines from its exclusive portfolio received scores of 91 points or higher from two of the wine world's most respected critics, Wine Enthusiast and James Suckling. The scores span three Kroger-exclusive labels and three price tiers, with the highest-rated bottle earning 93 points from James Suckling and the most affordable earning 92 points and a Best Buy designation from Wine Enthusiast , at just $7.99 a bottle. "These scores are a reminder that great wine does not have to come with a big price tag," said Curtis Mann, Master of Wine and vice president of adult beverage at Kroger. "We are obsessive about how we invest in sourcing and quality across our wine portfolio. Seeing that work validated by well-respected critics across multiple varietals and price points tells us we're getting it right." articles.title: Kroger wines earn elite scores at every price point

articles.summary: The Kroger Co. (NYSE: KR) will host an Investor Update today in New York, where company leaders will outline a multi-year plan to build America's Favorite Grocer and accelerate growth. The company also reiterates its guidance for full-year 2026 provided at its second quarter earnings. Comments from CEO Greg Foran "Kroger has a clear opportunity to unlock our full potential and build America's Favorite Grocer," said Greg Foran, CEO of Kroger. "We are making value more visible and focusing resources closer to the customer where we see the highest returns. With our customers at the center, we are simplifying and modernizing our business to deliver a great customer experience and provide long-term value to our shareholders." Building America's Favorite Grocer Kroger's updated strategy centers on three pillars, with a clear focus on execution and the customer at the center. articles.title: Kroger Outlines Plan to Build America's Favorite Grocer and Introduces New Long-Term Financial Targets

articles.summary: Halloween is one of America's most anticipated celebrations, and candy is at the center of it. This year, The Kroger Co. (NYSE: KR), America's grocer, expects to sell 25 million pounds of Halloween candy. Those sales will be made up of millions of pounds of chocolate, including nine million bags of fun-sized chocolate treats. If placed end-to-end, these bags would stretch 1,400 miles, the distance from Cincinnati to Salt Lake City. Kroger's Halloween assortment features everything from classic chocolate favorites and gummy treats to candy corn and limited-time offerings that trick-or-treaters of all ages will love. "Halloween is one of the most fun times of year for families and communities, and candy plays an important role," said Mike Murphy, group vice president for center store and merchandising at Kroger. "We want every customer to find what they are looking for, whether it's a full candy bowl for neighborhood kids, the perfect treat for a classroom party or a seasonal favorite."
articles.title: Kroger is America's candy destination

articles.summary: The Kroger Co. (NYSE: KR), America's grocer, shares that getting vaccinated is one of the most effective steps families can take to protect their health and the health of those around them. Kroger pharmacies make it easy to schedule a vaccine appointment alongside weekly errands. Flu, COVID-19, RSV and other routine vaccines are available now at Kroger Family of Pharmacies, with walk-in and scheduled appointments available. Most patients with health insurance can receive vaccines at no out-of-pocket costs. Vaccine appointments can be scheduled at Kroger.com/vaccine . Savings are automatically loaded to a customers' loyalty accounts at Kroger pharmacy locations. "Kroger touches more than 11 million customers every day, giving us a real opportunity to protect our communities," said Bill Shinton, interim president of Kroger Health. articles.title: Kroger helps keep families healthy this fall
